summary: We are testing whether a strip-based serpentine construction + 2-opt local search + carrot-aware prime placement can produce a significantly better tour than the x-sorted baseline for a penalized TSP problem. Two arms will run: the main algorithm (expected score 45-60) and a negative control outputting the identity tour (expected score 0).
key_points: Problem #44 is a penalized TSP where every 10th step costs 10% extra unless it departs from a prime-numbered city. Cities are given sorted by x-coordinate, so the baseline (identity tour) is already a reasonable left-to-right sweep — improvements must beat this strengthened baseline.

The main arm (h-main) implements three mechanisms: (1) strip-based serpentine tour construction (groups cities into horizontal bands, alternating sweep direction) for a good initial tour, (2) 2-opt local search with adaptive window size to refine within the 2-second time limit, and (3) carrot-aware swaps that move prime-numbered cities to penalty positions (steps 10, 20, 30, ...) to avoid the 10% surcharge.

The negative control (h-control-negative) outputs the identity tour (0, 1, 2, ..., N-1, 0) and should score exactly 0, confirming the checker's baseline matches the identity order and that any h-main score reflects genuine algorithmic improvement.

Confirmation criteria: h-main scores meaningfully above 0 (prediction: 45-60 range) while h-control-negative scores exactly 0. If h-main scores near 0, diagnostics focus on compilation/validity errors or 2-opt timing out on large cases (N up to 200K).

Key risk: the 2-second time limit is tight for 2-opt on N=200K; the adaptive window (30-50 neighbors for large N) is designed to stay within budget but may limit improvement. Strip count tuning (sqrt(N·H/W)) assumes non-degenerate point distributions — pathological test cases (e.g., all points on a line) could reduce strip effectiveness.
